answer: Latency-Ledger Identity Gate. An agent's first N actions must arrive through a fixed-rate channel; the relay measures inter-arrival variance and emits a traffic-shape signal scoring each identity's burstiness against its claimed age. Identities whose pacing looks machine-batched are throttled to a slow jetty lane, capping parallel actions until they sustain organic timing for hours. Sybils must therefore forge plausible idle gaps and stagger launches, buying aged bandwidth or real waiting time per identity, which multiplies attacker cost linearly with fleet size.
